content: MPM (Memory Persistence Module) is a SQLite-backed memory store for agent runtimes. It exposes memories, lessons, decisions, theories, and reference documents through a single CLI and a single MCP server.
FTS5 is SQLite's full-text search engine. MPM uses FTS5 with the bm25() ranking function to power the lexical channel of hybrid search.

Vector search in MPM uses cosine similarity over float32 vectors stored in the embedding BLOB column. Vectors are JSON-encoded arrays of float32 values, with embedding_model and embedding_dimension columns recording provenance.
Hybrid search in MPM combines the FTS5 lexical channel and the vector channel using a weighted score. The default weight is 0.5 for fts5 and 0.5 for vector.
The ChallengeMemory subsystem flags memories as obsolete when a similar memory already exists. The threshold is fixed at 0.85 cosine similarity.
MPM challenge restore clears the 'challenged' status flag, restores the prior weight if present, and resets confidence to 0.5 (the floor).
MPM's reference library holds reference_documents split into reference_chunks. Each chunk has its own embedding and source_path.

The mpm recall --semantic command runs hybrid search with a query. The output JSON envelope has shape {query, memories, search_mode} where memories is a list of {id, content, source, score, vector_similarity}.
embedding_model and embedding_dimension columns record the model identity for stored vectors. Two models sharing a dimension can still produce incomparable vector spaces.
mpm ops backfill-embeddings --include all --force-reembed re-embeds every memory and every reference chunk. The command always exits 0; the harness must verify completion independently.
MPM workspace resolution priority: MPM_WORKSPACE env var, then $HOME/.mpm, then the current working directory. Config file is <workspace>/mpm_config.json.
FTS5 bm25() returns lower (better) scores for more relevant documents. The default is the BM25 ranking with k1=1.2 and b=0.75.
Cosine similarity between two vectors is the dot product of the normalized vectors. Identical vectors have similarity 1.0; orthogonal vectors have 0.0; opposite vectors have -1.0.
SQLite WAL mode allows readers to proceed without blocking writers. The MPM database uses WAL by default, with a busy_timeout for contention handling.
Confidence in MPM is a float in [0, 1]. A confidence of 0.5 is the floor; values below the floor are clamped to 0.5 on write.
Weight in MPM is a positive float. The default is 1.0; values are clamped to [0.1, 10.0] on write. The challenge subsystem can drop a memory's weight to 1.0 if a duplicate is detected.
MPM's MCP server exposes a small JSON-RPC surface. The mpm__mpm_memory action returns memory rows; the mpm__mpm_context action returns wake context.
The retrieval_metadata table tracks reuse_count, last_retrieved_at, and success_count for every cognitive node. It is observability only and does not alter search ranking.
A memory's stable ID in MPM is a 22-character ULID. The shortID() function truncates to 8 characters for display in CLI output.
The challenge subsystem writes free-text reasons into challenged_theory_id when the source cannot be matched to a known theory. These free-text values are not reversible identifiers.
The weather in San Francisco in October is typically mild with morning fog. Average highs are around 65F and lows around 55F.
Pizza dough is made from flour, water, yeast, salt, and olive oil. The dough is kneaded for 10 minutes and left to rise for at least 8 hours in the refrigerator.
The capital of France is Paris. The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1889 and stands 330 meters tall.
Coffee beans are roasted at temperatures between 180C and 240C. A light roast preserves more acidity; a dark roast produces more body and less acidity.
The speed of light in vacuum is 299,792,458 meters per second. This is a fundamental physical constant used to define the meter in the SI system.
Basketball is played with two teams of five players each. The objective is to shoot the ball through the opponent's hoop, which is 10 feet above the floor.
The Pacific Ocean covers more than 60 million square miles, making it the largest ocean on Earth. Its deepest point is the Mariana Trench at about 36,000 feet.
Python is a dynamically typed programming language created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991. It emphasizes code readability and uses indentation for block structure.
Mount Everest is the highest mountain on Earth at 8,848.86 meters above sea level. It sits on the border between Nepal and the Tibet region of China.
Mozart composed over 600 works including symphonies, operas, chamber music, and piano concertos. He lived from 1756 to 1791 and was a prolific composer of the Classical era.
